newsitem.title: DENMARK: Dollar and Dow seen damping Danish shares.
newsitem.headline: Dollar and Dow seen damping Danish shares.

text.p: Danish share prices fell on Friday, with the weak dollar, falling Dow and forthcoming major Danish company interim results likely to get the Copenhagen market off to a nervous start next week.

"I think there will be good performance in side paper but it is not certain that that will be enough to move the KFX index. There will be a lot of uncertainty ahead of the major KFX companies' accounts," a dealer said.
The KFX top-20 index fell 1.87 point to 181.99 in overall bourse turnover of 1.183 billion crowns. Its September future fell 0.2 to 181.80 with 293 contracts of 100,000 crowns traded.
Among firms publishing first-half results next week are the country's top three banks, Den Danske Bank, Unibank and BG Bank.
All are expecting bumper profits, but that was not enough to cushion them from Friday's dollar-driven falls.
Den Danske closed four crowns down, at 708.00, Unibank also fell four crowns, to 421.00 and BG Bank lost three, to close at 392.00.
One of only two KFX shares to rise was Radiometer, which publishes full-year results on Monday. It rose five crowns to 335.00.
A.P. Moeller's D/S Svendborg rose 416.6 crowns, to 425,416.66. REUTER
